newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish PM to unveil second resource package.
newsitem.headline: Turkish PM to unveil second resource package.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan will unveil on Thursday the government's second revenue-raising package aimed at generating $10 billion to fight deficits, the PM's press office said.
It said Erbakan would present the package in a joint press conference with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, scheduled to begin at 0800 GMT.

The package is expected to contain short-term privatisation plans, securitisation of state real estate and a central cash management system to "pool" public revenues in a single account to help poor state firms.
Brokers at Istanbul's stock exchange said the market was likely to pay attention to privatisation details in the package.

The first package, disclosed on July 31, included speeding up sell-offs, issuing foreign-currency denominated bonds, selling state property, incentives and tax exemptions for Turkish workers abroad to channel their savings into the country and a six-percent charge on the financing of some imports.

The government aims to raise $10 billion each from the two packages in the next three years, but the first package has failed to raise optimism in the business community and markets which saw it as impractical.
